summary:
President Donald Trump used his UN General Assembly speech to defend the US-Israeli war against Iran, threaten to “annihilate” the country and say a deal remained possible. His remarks put the conflict at the centre of a gathering where leaders typically present themselves as advocates of peace. Iran’s next steps and the prospect of negotiations remain uncertain.

Typhoon Dujuan brought record rain, landslides and power outages to Japan, killing at least four people, with one report putting the toll at five. Tens of thousands faced evacuation orders as rescuers searched for missing people. In Sri Lanka, a High Court convicted 15 men over the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings, while nine defendants were acquitted; the attacks killed hundreds and targeted churches and hotels.

The US, Denmark and Greenland signed a deal allowing a larger US military presence on the island, including at least two new bases, in an effort to ease tensions over its strategic importance. Separately, a UN human rights investigator said US strikes on alleged drug boats may violate international law. British Columbia has sued OpenAI over its handling of concerns about the Tumbler Ridge school shooter, while the EU removed two Russian oligarchs from its sanctions list. The UK also offered defensive air support to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks.

headlines.title: Trump threatens Iran in UN speech and says a deal remains possible
headlines.summary: At the UN General Assembly, President Donald Trump defended the US-Israeli war against Iran and warned that he could “annihilate” the country, while saying a deal remained possible. His remarks leave uncertainty over the next steps in the conflict and drew attention from other world leaders.

headlines.title: Typhoon kills at least four in Japan and brings record rain
headlines.summary: Typhoon Dujuan brought heavy rain, landslides and power outages to Japan, killing at least four people; another report put the death toll at five. Tens of thousands of people faced evacuation orders as rescuers searched for the missing and authorities warned of further flooding and landslides.

headlines.title: Sri Lankan court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings
headlines.summary: A Sri Lankan High Court convicted 15 men over the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings, while nine of the 24 accused were acquitted. The attacks targeted churches and hotels, killing hundreds; the verdict marks a major step in the case against those accused of direct involvement.

headlines.title: US deal with Denmark and Greenland expands American military presence
headlines.summary: The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an agreement allowing a larger US military presence on the strategically located island, including at least two new bases. The deal comes after tensions over Trump’s push for greater US control of Greenland.

headlines.title: UN expert says US strikes on alleged drug boats may violate law
headlines.summary: A UN human rights investigator said there are reasonable grounds to believe US attacks on boats alleged to carry drugs may constitute crimes against humanity. The assessment adds to legal scrutiny of the strikes, which the report says have killed more than 230 people since September 2025.

headlines.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI over school shooting
headlines.summary: British Columbia sued OpenAI, alleging the company should have warned police about concerns related to the shooter’s use of ChatGPT before a mass shooting at a school in Tumbler Ridge. The case puts the company’s safety practices and obligations to alert authorities under legal scrutiny.

headlines.title: EU removes two Russian oligarchs from sanctions list
headlines.summary: The EU removed Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 other people and entities. Ukraine had argued the bloc should increase pressure on Moscow, and the decision was described by Ireland’s EU presidency as a difficult compromise.

headlines.title: UK offers defensive support to Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
headlines.summary: The UK said it would provide defensive air support to Saudi Arabia as it faces Houthi attacks; the G7 has also called on the Houthis to stop attacks on civilian shipping. The move is one of Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s first significant military decisions and signals a UK role in the regional response.
